title: Small-ball bound for Gaussian polynomials
statement:
There is a constant $K>0$ such that, for every pair of natural numbers $n,k$ with $1\le k$, every real polynomial $p$ in $n$ variables of total degree at most $k$ whose squared value has integral $1$ under the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures, and every $\varepsilon>0$, one has
\[
\gamma_n\bigl(\{z:|p(z)|\le\varepsilon\}\bigr)\le Kk\,\varepsilon^{1/k},
\]
where $\gamma_n$ denotes that product Gaussian measure.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real polynomial in $n$ variables
The total degree of $p$ is at most $k$
